title: Blade OML angular position at the -7 deg (low-pitch) end stop, hub A datum to blade OML, worst-case sensitivity (degrees)

checks.label: Blade-pitch angular position variation margin against S461-607, at the -7 deg end stop

configuration.sensitivity_condition: worst-case (source sheet D10/D11, stated at -5 deg)

source_ref.callout: The pitch angle of each blade in a propeller assembly shall not exceed +/-0.5 degrees of the mean pitch of the blades
source_ref.note: c_status: draft. Pulled 2026-09-06 from Polarion (Delta mirror, manufacturing.polarion.workitem); severity must_have. This is a blade-to-blade variation limit, not a limit on this chain's own accumulated position error -- adopted here as the closest available numeric acceptance criterion for the accumulated tolerance this study folds, because S461-241 states only the two nominal stop angles and S461-805's own threshold is TBD (see excluded_terms).

context_ref.callout: The propeller assembly shall provide propeller pitch end stops at -7º and +72º.
context_ref.note: c_status: draft. Pulled 2026-09-06. Names the nominal operating point this study represents (-7 deg); not itself a numeric criterion, so not folded into the check -- carried as the context a reader needs to know WHY this study exists, per SourceRef.kind 'requirement'.

excluded_terms: hub top deck to actuator mounting face (edge hub_top_deck_to_vpa_mount) -- no source document, `assumed` placeholder
actuator mounting face to end-stop feature (edge vpa_mount_to_end_stop_feature) -- no source document, `assumed` placeholder

piston end to end-stop feature (edge end_stop_clearance) -- THE end stop itself; a real drawing candidate exists (214700-002-A sheet 2, `5.00 +/-0.05`) but its feature identity is not established (WORKSHEET_endstop_vision_baseline.md §8b row 39, 'candidate (strong)'), so it stays `untraced`
blade root to OML (edge blade_root_clocking_to_oml) -- not a drawing quantity at all; the source workbook's own author doubts the number by roughly 6x (row 22, 'Probably closer to .03deg')

the -5 deg sensitivity this study borrows (transform pitch_arm_linear_to_rotary, source cell D10) is 2 deg off the -7 deg this check is actually about, and the source cell itself names three different operating conditions around one number (WORKSHEET_end_stop_graft.md finding F1) -- no sensitivity constant characterised AT -7 deg exists in any source this repo holds

gas-spring bushing tipping backlash -- the source workbook's largest single angular contributor (0.72 deg, its row 68) and not represented as a chain edge at all (see this topology's own notes, 'WHAT THIS TOPOLOGY CANNOT REPRODUCE')

S461-805 (Blade Pitch Position Accuracy) states its own threshold as literally 'TBD deg' in Polarion -- draft, no usable numeric criterion, so it supplies no check of its own and is not folded into this one either

provenance.why_this_study_exists: S461-241 (draft, 'End stop') requires the propeller assembly to provide pitch end stops at -7 deg and +72 deg -- the two nominal operating points the source workbook's own D-column/F-column sensitivity split approximates without ever landing on either exactly. This study is `pitch_system_blade_angle_worst`'s exact selection and transform set, re-titled and re-scoped as the -7 deg stop's study and given a requirement-cited check, per the handoff's item 1 ('one study per stop direction'). It is a SEPARATE document from that study -- not an edit of it -- because the handoff's baseline forbids touching the four existing pitch-system study documents' numbers.
provenance.the_condition_mismatch_named: The source sheet's D10/D11 sensitivity pair is documented at '-5 deg (worst case)' (D10's own cell comment), not -7 deg. A 2 degree gap between the requirement's operating point and the only sensitivity constant this repo holds is a real, unresolved finding -- not glossed over by reusing the closer of the two available conditions. Recorded in the check's `excluded_terms` (not just here) so it renders on the card, and in the lesson as a new finding.

notes: Selection and transforms are byte-for-byte identical to study_pitch_system_blade_angle_worst.json's; only the id, title, provenance and the added `checks` entry differ. Comparing the two files' totals is therefore a no-op by construction -- the point of this document is the check, not a new number.

complete: false is the honest outcome the handoff's definition of done asks for: the chain crosses two `assumed` placeholders and one `candidate`-identity edge (the end stop itself), and the requirement this check's numeric limit borrows (S461-607) is not the requirement that names this study's own operating point (S461-241). None of that is a licence to skip publishing the number -- it is why the number renders as a budget, never a hardware verdict.
